title: Array methods for data
lesson:
Apps are mostly data in, summaries out: total kg per crop, the five top scorers, which medicines are running low. You met `map`, `filter` and `reduce` in Level 1. Here they become your everyday tools, joined by `find`, `some`, `every` and `sort`. Each takes a small function and does the looping for you, which means fewer off-by-one bugs and code that says *what* it does.

```
const harvests = [{ farmer: "Amina", crop: "maize", kg: 120 }, ...];

harvests.map((h) => h.kg)                  // change each: [120, 45, ...]
harvests.filter((h) => h.crop === "maize") // keep some
harvests.find((h) => h.farmer === "Juma")  // the FIRST match, or undefined
harvests.some((h) => h.kg > 100)           // is any true?
harvests.every((h) => h.kg > 0)            // are all true?
harvests.reduce((sum, h) => sum + h.kg, 0) // combine into one value
```

**reduce into an object** groups and totals in one pass:

```
const perCrop = harvests.reduce((totals, h) => {
  totals[h.crop] = (totals[h.crop] || 0) + h.kg;
  return totals;                 // always return the running value
}, {});                          // start with an empty object
```

Always give `reduce` a starting value (`0`, `{}`, `[]`). Without one, an empty array throws an error, and that's the day the clinic has no data yet.

**Sorting** needs a *compare function* that returns a negative number if a comes first, positive if b comes first, and 0 if they tie:

```
[...rows].sort((a, b) => a.kg - b.kg)                 // small to big
[...rows].sort((a, b) => b.kg - a.kg)                 // big to small
[...rows].sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))  // A to Z
[...rows].sort((a, b) => b.kg - a.kg || a.name.localeCompare(b.name))  // ties broken by name
```

Two traps: without a compare function, `sort` compares as *text*, so `[10, 9, 100]` becomes `[10, 100, 9]`. And `sort` **changes the array it's called on**. Copy first with `[...rows]` so you don't reorder data other code relies on.

**Chaining** reads like a sentence: `harvests.filter((h) => h.crop === "beans").map((h) => h.farmer)` is "the farmers who grew beans". `Object.entries(perCrop)` turns `{ maize: 200 }` into `[["maize", 200]]`, so an object of totals can be sorted and mapped too.

One more trap: an arrow with braces needs `return`. `(h) => { h.kg * 2 }` returns undefined; write `(h) => h.kg * 2`, or `{ return h.kg * 2; }`. For an object, wrap it in brackets: `(h) => ({ crop: h.crop })`.

notes: reduce with 0 sums; reduce with {} groups.
Copy with [...] before sort; ties are broken by name with ||.
map also gives the position (i), handy for ranks.
find returns the first match; some answers yes or no.

exercises.title: Totals per crop
exercises.prompt: Harvests look like [{ farmer: "Amina", crop: "maize", kg: 120 }, ...]. Write totalsPerCrop(harvests) returning an object of total kg per crop (use reduce), grandTotal(harvests) returning all the kg added up, and cropsOver(harvests, kg) returning the names of crops whose TOTAL is more than kg, sorted A to Z.

tests.call: totalsPerCrop([{ farmer: "Amina", crop: "maize", kg: 120 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 45 }, { farmer: "Wanjiru", crop: "maize", kg: 80 }, { farmer: "Otieno", crop: "potatoes", kg: 60 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 30 }])
tests.name: totals per crop

tests.call: grandTotal([{ farmer: "Amina", crop: "maize", kg: 120 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 45 }, { farmer: "Wanjiru", crop: "maize", kg: 80 }, { farmer: "Otieno", crop: "potatoes", kg: 60 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 30 }])
tests.name: grand total

tests.call: cropsOver([{ farmer: "Amina", crop: "maize", kg: 120 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 45 }, { farmer: "Wanjiru", crop: "maize", kg: 80 }, { farmer: "Otieno", crop: "potatoes", kg: 60 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 30 }], 60)
tests.name: crops over 60 kg, A to Z
tests.hint_if_fail: More than, not equal: potatoes has exactly 60.

tests.name: no harvests yet
tests.hint_if_fail: Give reduce a starting value: 0 or {}.

hints: harvests.reduce((totals, h) => { totals[h.crop] = (totals[h.crop] || 0) + h.kg; return totals; }, {})

exercises.title: Sort and find
exercises.prompt: Write sortByKg(harvests): a NEW array (the original keeps its order) sorted by kg from most to least, with ties sorted by farmer name A to Z. Write findFarmer(harvests, name): the first harvest whose farmer matches name ignoring upper/lower case and spaces around name, or null if there is none.

tests.call: sortByKg([{ farmer: "Amina", crop: "maize", kg: 120 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 45 }, { farmer: "Wanjiru", crop: "maize", kg: 80 }, { farmer: "Otieno", crop: "potatoes", kg: 60 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 30 }]).map((h) => h.farmer)
tests.name: most to least

tests.call: findFarmer([{ farmer: "Amina", crop: "maize", kg: 120 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 45 }, { farmer: "Wanjiru", crop: "maize", kg: 80 }, { farmer: "Otieno", crop: "potatoes", kg: 60 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 30 }], "juma")
tests.name: find ignoring case

tests.call: findFarmer([{ farmer: "Amina", crop: "maize", kg: 120 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 45 }, { farmer: "Wanjiru", crop: "maize", kg: 80 }, { farmer: "Otieno", crop: "potatoes", kg: 60 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 30 }], "Zawadi")
tests.name: not found gives null
tests.hint_if_fail: find gives undefined when nothing matches; turn that into null.

tests.call: sortByKg([{ farmer: "Wanjiru", kg: 50 }, { farmer: "Amina", kg: 50 }, { farmer: "Juma", kg: 70 }]).map((h) => h.farmer)
tests.name: ties A to Z
the original isn't reordered

tests.call: findFarmer([{ farmer: "Amina", crop: "maize", kg: 120 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 45 }, { farmer: "Wanjiru", crop: "maize", kg: 80 }, { farmer: "Otieno", crop: "potatoes", kg: 60 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 30 }], "  WANJIRU ").kg
tests.name: spaces and capitals

exercises.title: A season report
exercises.prompt: Write report(harvests, prices). prices is an object of KSh per kg, like { maize: 50, beans: 120 }. Return an array with one object per crop: { crop, kg, ksh } where kg is the crop's total and ksh = kg times its price (0 if the crop has no price). Sort by ksh from most to least, ties by crop A to Z. Also write topFarmers(harvests, n): the names of the n farmers with the most total kg (one farmer can have several harvests), most first, ties A to Z.

tests.call: report([{ farmer: "Amina", crop: "maize", kg: 120 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 45 }, { farmer: "Wanjiru", crop: "maize", kg: 80 }, { farmer: "Otieno", crop: "potatoes", kg: 60 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 30 }], { maize: 50, beans: 120 }).map((r) => [r.crop, r.kg, r.ksh])
tests.name: the report

tests.call: topFarmers([{ farmer: "Amina", crop: "maize", kg: 120 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 45 }, { farmer: "Wanjiru", crop: "maize", kg: 80 }, { farmer: "Otieno", crop: "potatoes", kg: 60 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 30 }], 2)
tests.name: top two farmers
tests.hint_if_fail: Juma has two harvests: 45 + 30 = 75, less than Wanjiru's 80.

tests.call: topFarmers([{ farmer: "Amina", crop: "maize", kg: 120 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 45 }, { farmer: "Wanjiru", crop: "maize", kg: 80 }, { farmer: "Otieno", crop: "potatoes", kg: 60 }, { farmer: "Juma", crop: "beans", kg: 30 }], 10)
tests.name: asking for more than there are

tests.call: report([{ farmer: "A", crop: "beans", kg: 10 }, { farmer: "B", crop: "rice", kg: 5 }], { beans: 20, rice: 40 }).map((r) => r.crop)
tests.name: ties by crop name

hints: First total the kg per crop with reduce into an object.
Object.entries(kgByCrop).map(([crop, kg]) => ({ crop, kg, ksh: kg * (prices[crop] || 0) }))
topFarmers: total per farmer, Object.entries, sort, slice(0, n), map to the name.

quiz.why: With no compare function, sort compares as text.

choices: sort changes the array it's called on; the copy protects the original
quiz.why: Sorting in place can surprise other code using the same array.

quiz.q: [].reduce((s, x) => s + x) with no starting value…
quiz.why: Always pass a starting value: reduce(fn, 0).
With braces you need return; or drop the braces.

quiz.q: You need the first patient older than 70, or nothing. Which method?
quiz.why: find stops at the first match and returns it (or undefined).

cards.a: rows.reduce((t, r) => { t[r.k] = (t[r.k] || 0) + r.v; return t; }, {})

explain: Explain what a compare function for sort returns, and write one for a made-up leaderboard.
